operations.name: Bogus Bylines
operations.summary: Iran-origin operation that used seven invented journalist bylines to pitch long-form articles about the US-Iran conflict to small and medium online outlets. OpenAI identified almost 100 articles published or syndicated under the bylines across roughly a dozen outlets between July 2025 and October 2026 and assessed the activity as consistent with a for-hire commercial actor. NPR, citing NBC News, reported that Middle East Monitor published at least 21 articles by four of the personas and that one persona posted in the Daily Kos community section. The outlets were deceived and are not fronts.

operations.name: Dark Clark
operations.summary: Russia-origin operation targeting Latin America that controlled a self-styled research platform, the Social Research Center, through a fake persona named Mia Clark, and claimed to have planted fake stories in Peruvian, Polish, Ecuadorian and Bolivian media. OpenAI assessed it at Category 5 on the IO Breakout Scale and tied parts of it to reporting on the Russian entity known as Politology or La Compania.

operations.name: Alice Donovan (precedent)
operations.summary: Precedent named in the OpenAI report of 8 October 2026: the fake journalist Alice Donovan, a front for Russian military intelligence whose articles were published by a range of Western outlets in 2016 and 2017. The persona ceased activity after exposure.

operations.name: PeaceData
operations.reported_by: NBC News, citing Facebook and Graphika
operations.summary: Fake news outlet Peace Data, run by people formerly associated with the Russian Internet Research Agency according to Facebook, which recruited unwitting freelance writers through fictional editor personas. Also named as a precedent in the OpenAI report of 8 October 2026.

operations.name: Iran-linked Arabic bylines
operations.summary: The Daily Beast reported that three fictitious journalists published articles in dozens of periodicals and news websites since May 2019, and that Facebook attributed the amplification to trolls based in Iran using fake accounts. Meta's December 2020 Coordinated Inauthentic Behavior report (https://about.fb.com/news/2021/01/december-2020-coordinated-inauthentic-behavior-report/) lists a small Iran network found after reviewing information from FireEye and The Daily Beast and notes networks that targeted traditional media to place stories under fictitious bylines.

operations.name: HaiEnergy
operations.summary: Pro-PRC information operation using at least 72 suspected inauthentic news sites, which Mandiant linked by technical indicators to Shanghai Haixun Technology Co., Ltd, a Chinese public relations firm. Mandiant did not establish the extent of Haixun's knowledge of the campaign and did not attribute it directly to the PRC government.

operations.name: HaiEnergy newswires and US news subdomains
operations.summary: Follow-up report finding HaiEnergy content distributed through two self-described press release services, Times Newswire and World Newswire, and placed on at least 32 subdomains of legitimate US news outlets that resolved to infrastructure of FinancialContent, Inc. Mandiant saw no evidence that the affected outlets were compromised and did not establish a technical connection between Haixun and the newswires.

operations.name: Paperwall
operations.summary: Network of at least 123 websites in 30 countries posing as local news outlets and mixing pro-Beijing content and attacks on critics into commercial press releases. Citizen Lab attributed the network to Shenzhen Haimaiyunxiang Media Co., Ltd., known as Haimai, on the basis of infrastructure links, and published the full list of 123 domains.

operations.name: GlassBridge
operations.summary: Google described four China-based public relations and marketing firms, Shanghai Haixun Technology, Shenzhen Haimai Yunxiang Media, DURINBRIDGE and Shenzhen Bowen Media, running inauthentic news sites and newswire services that spread pro-PRC content. Google blocked more than a thousand of their sites from Google News and Discover since 2022 and assessed that the firms may take direction from a shared customer it could not identify.

operations.name: The Swiss biologist that never was
operations.summary: A fake persona called Wilson Edwards, claiming to be a Swiss biologist, posted on 24 July 2021 that the United States was pressuring WHO scientists over COVID-19 origins. Within a week Chinese state media including the Global Times and People's Daily ran headlines on the claim; the Swiss embassy in Beijing said no such citizen existed. Meta linked the operation to individuals in mainland China including employees of Sichuan Silence Information Technology Co, Ltd and to employees of Chinese state infrastructure companies abroad.
